definition: Ultrafast is OpenAI's premium speed tier, announced at DevDay 2026. It generates tokens — the chunks of text a model produces — up to eight times faster in Codex and up to six times faster in the API. OpenAI quotes about 300 tokens per second in Codex, where a fast human reader manages maybe four or five words a second. The catch is the price: GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast costs $60 per million input tokens and $300 per million output, six times Astra's standard $10 and $50. In ChatGPT, Ultrafast comes with the new $500-a-month Pro 500 plan.

edges.label: measured in tokens per second
edges.note: Speed tiers are priced by how fast tokens stream out, so tokens are the unit of both speed and cost.

edges.label: six times faster spend
edges.note: Fast tokens still cost tokens — a run that takes minutes at standard speed burns the same usage in seconds.

edges.label: agents feel instant
edges.note: At this speed an agentic loop's pauses nearly vanish — a different product from the user's point of view.

example.body: During the keynote, Romain Huet typed into a demo running at Ultrafast speed and the answer poured out — genuinely startling. Then the meter: the same answer that costs pennies at standard speed costs six times more. Testers called the demos mind-blowing, “but also wallet-blowing.” That's the whole trade-off in one sentence: time or money, pick one.
example.title: The demo that empties the tank

footnotes.body: At launch, GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast was available in the API and in ChatGPT Work and Codex on Pro 500 and Enterprise plans; GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast was described as “coming soon.” In ChatGPT, Pro 500 costs $500/month with a usage allowance OpenAI describes as 25 times ChatGPT Plus. Speed tiers are a snapshot of pricing — they change.
footnotes.label: Availability and pricing

name: Ultrafast
tagline: OpenAI's premium speed tier: up to 8x faster token generation — at roughly 6x the price.
whyItMatters: Speed changes what an agent feels like: a background agent that answers in seconds instead of minutes is a different product. But speed multiplies the token bill just as fast — Ultrafast makes the economics of agentic loops visible in a single number.
